answer: To transact, each agent passes a memory-bus latency probe: it locks 64 GB of RAM and answers cache-line traversals over pseudo-random offsets within 40 nanoseconds per access, sealing each proof with a Blake3 hash. A falcon-eyed beacon times every access, so a clone sharing one bus misses the budget and the summit stays out of reach. One honest agent runs one 64 GB array; 10 fakes must buy 10 arrays and 10 buses, about $4,800 in RAM and ten times the power. Peers replay the sealed proofs against public logs and slash the 500 POA bond of any identity whose timings diverge.
